routes.name: Short stay without a visa (Schengen rules)
routes.summary: EU citizens need no visa. Some other nationalities are visa-exempt under the EU list, and others need a visa before entry. Stays are limited to 90 days in any 180.

other: The exact visa-exempt country list and the 90 day rule for exempt nationals were not confirmed on the page. Check the EU list linked from gov.si.

routes.name: EU citizen right to live in Slovenia
routes.summary: EU citizens enter with an ID card or passport and need no visa or residence permit. For longer stays they register for a residence registration certificate.

routes.name: Short stay visa (type C)
routes.summary: Third-country nationals who are not visa-exempt need a visa or residence permit before entering Slovenia for tourism, business or personal visits. Holders of a Schengen visa or residence permit from another Schengen country can enter within the 90 in 180 day limit.

other: Fees, documents and processing times were not read. Check a Slovenian embassy.

routes.name: Temporary residence permit for digital nomads
routes.summary: A one year permit for non-EU remote workers employed by or contracting with a business outside Slovenia, or self-employed abroad. Available since 21 November 2025. It can't be extended, but you can reapply six months after it expires.

other: Work remotely for a business based outside Slovenia, or be self-employed abroad.
You may not work on the Slovenian labor market.
Monthly funds of at least twice the average monthly net salary in Slovenia (euro figure not on the page). Any lawful income source counts.

stay.note: Reapply six months after expiry. You can apply for another permit type at any time while valid.

steps: Apply at a Slovenian embassy or consulate, or at an administrative unit if you are already legally in Slovenia.
Prove income of at least twice the average monthly net salary.

routes.name: Single permit for residence and work
routes.summary: Combined residence and work permit tied to an employer. Valid for the contract length, up to two years, with extensions up to three years in total.

eligibility.education: Education or qualifications matching the job
other: Valid passport, health insurance, sufficient means and a clean criminal record certificate.
Employment Service of Slovenia consent where required.
Listed shortage occupations get a fast-track procedure.

stay.note: Extensions up to three years in total.

steps: You or your employer apply at a Slovenian mission abroad or an administrative unit if lawfully in Slovenia.
Employment Service consent is obtained and a decision is issued.
Employer registers you for insurance within 15 days of collection.
Register your address at the administrative unit.
documents: Employer statement on business-reason dismissals in the last six months

routes.name: EU Blue Card
routes.summary: Residence and work permit for highly qualified employees. Issued for the contract length plus three months, up to two years, and extendable up to three years.

other: Salary and education thresholds were not on the page. Check infotujci.si.

stay.note: Contract length plus three months, max two years, extendable up to three.

routes.name: Residence for family of EU or Slovenian citizens
routes.summary: Non-EU spouses, registered partners, children up to 21 and some dependants of EU or Slovenian citizens can stay 90 days without a permit. For longer, apply for a residence permit before the 90 days end.

other: Covers spouse or partner, children up to 21 and certain dependants. Fees and documents not confirmed.

routes.name: Family reunification with a digital nomad
routes.summary: Family of a digital nomad permit holder can join right away. There is no waiting period tied to how long the holder has been in Slovenia.

other: Sponsor must hold the Slovenian digital nomad permit.

routes.name: Residence for study
routes.summary: Third-country nationals who study in Slovenia need a visa or residence permit before entering. Study time counts for half toward permanent residence.

other: Admission, funds and fee details were not read.

routes.name: Permanent residence permit
routes.summary: Standard route is five years of continuous legal residence on a temporary permit with regular sufficient income. Blue Card holders need five years in the EU, the last two in Slovenia. Family of permanent residents need two years.

other: Valid travel document and regular sufficient income.
Seasonal work, posted work, intra-company transfers and temporary protection do not count toward the period.
Language requirement was not on the page. Check infotujci.si.

routes.name: Citizenship by naturalization
routes.summary: General rule is 10 years in Slovenia, including 5 continuous years right before applying. Shorter periods apply to refugees, graduates of Slovenian higher education and some others.

eligibility.language: Slovenian language exam (details not on the page)
other: Stateless people and refugees: 5 continuous years.
Higher education in Slovenia: 7 years including 1 continuous year.

citizenship.note: Slovenia doesn't automatically revoke citizenship when someone gains another, but proof of release from the old citizenship is generally required. EU citizens with reciprocity, stateless people and minors are exempt.

routes.name: Citizenship by marriage
routes.summary: Spouse of a Slovenian citizen: married at least 3 years and at least 1 continuous year of residence in Slovenia before applying.

eligibility.language: Slovenian language exam (details not on the page)

routes.name: Citizenship for Slovenian descendants
routes.summary: Slovenian expatriates and descendants up to the fourth degree in a direct line need 1 continuous year of residence. Those up to the second degree who meet extra conditions may skip the residence requirement.

other: Second degree route needs several years of personal ties to Slovenia and at least five years of involvement in Slovenian organizations abroad.

citizenship.note: Up to the fourth degree in a direct line.
